### Observed differences

- Activity A01 is absent from the earlier window (0 of 200 traces) but appears exactly once per trace in about 48 in 100 traces in the later window, late among the trace's event positions (median relative position about 0.85). [OCC001, POS001]
- In the earlier window, A18's outgoing transitions spread over many activities (largest single share about 19 in 100, to A10) and never went to A01; in the later window, about 65 in 100 of A18's outgoing transitions go to A01. [DIR004]
- The pair A01–A18 never co-occurred earlier (A18 appeared without A01 in about 40 in 100 traces); in the later window the two co-occur in about 48 in 100 traces, always with A18 before A01. [REL001]
- In the later window, A01's observed outgoing transitions fan out widely — about 17 in 100 to A10, 15 to A07, 14 to A12, and about 12 each to A16 and A17 — largely the same activities A18 previously led to directly. [DIR001, DIR004]
- A02 now repeats: participation is similar (about 48 vs 54 in 100 traces), but mean occurrences per trace roughly doubled (about 0.48 to 1.01) and repetition appears in about 26 in 100 traces, against none earlier. [OCC002]
- A08 repeats less: participation is stable (about 47 in 100 traces in both windows), but mean occurrences fell from about 0.87 to about 0.48 (once per trace) and repetition support dropped from 0.20 to 0. [OCC003]
- Routing shifted toward A02 and away from A08: about 65 in 100 of A09's outgoing transitions now go to A02 (about 38 earlier), while A07 is no longer observed as a successor of A09; A14 now leads to A08 in about 24 in 100 of its transitions (about 63 earlier) and to A15 in about 19 (not observed earlier). [DIR002, DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that a new activity, A01, was added late in the process in the later window: it runs once in about 48 in 100 traces, after A18 — A18 precedes it in every co-occurrence, and about 65 in 100 of A18's outgoing transitions now lead to it — and it is followed by a spread of activities (A10, A07, A12, A16, A17, among others) that largely matches the successors A18 had before. [OCC001, POS001, REL001, DIR004, DIR001]

The change is shown directly by participation (0 of 200 traces earlier vs about 95 of 200 later), by the new A18→A01 link and the A18-before-A01 ordering, and by A01's outgoing profile, which exists only in the later window; the screening produced 9 qualifying items against about 0.2 expected if nothing had changed, so this set of differences is unlikely under a no-change scenario. The five A01-related items describe facets of one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations, and zero participation earlier strictly means only that A01 was not observed then. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude is that A01 existed earlier at a very low frequency that the 200-trace sample missed, although 0 of 200 traces makes a substantial earlier presence implausible. [OCC001, REL001, DIR001, DIR004]

Other differences: A02 repeats in about 26 in 100 traces (none earlier) with roughly double the mean occurrences per trace; A08 no longer repeats (repetition support 0.20 to 0, about one occurrence per trace); A09 leads to A02 more often (about 38 to 65 in 100) and no longer to A07; A14 leads less to A08 (about 63 to 24 in 100) and more to A15 and A06. The evidence does not directly tie these repetition and routing shifts to the arrival of A01. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR003]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 40 units tested, 9 items qualified, 0.2 expected without change. 9 items is many times larger than 0.2 — so the count cannot be explained by chance. All items are control-flow family. So we move past the screening comparison and judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

Evidence items (9 total):
1. OCC001: A01 — before: 0 occurrences, 0 participation; after: mean 0.475, participation 0.475 (95/200 traces). A01 appeared in the later window; not observed before. Empirical strength 0.995.
2. OCC002: A02 — before: mean 0.48, participation 0.48, recurrence 0; after: mean 1.01, participation 0.54, recurrence 0.255. A02 became repeated in some traces (recurrence support 0.255 → about 51 of 200 traces? Actually recurrence_support 0.255 — share of traces with repetition? Support after 108 traces contain A02). Mean occurrences per trace rose from ~0.48 to ~1.01, so about doubled; participation roughly stable (48% → 54%), so repetitions increased.
3. OCC003: A08 — before: mean 0.87, participation 0.465, recurrence 0.2; after: mean 0.475, participation 0.475, recurrence 0. A08 stopped repeating: before ~47% of traces contained it with mean 0.87 (some repeats), after ~48% contain it but mean 0.475 (exactly once each). So A08 became single-occurrence.
4. DIR001: A01 outgoing — before empty (A01 not observed), after: outgoing transitions to A10 (17%), A07 (15%), A12 (14%), A16 (12%), A17 (12%), A13 (8%), A06 (10%), A11 (5%), A19 (5%), A02 (2%). Support after 59 (outgoing transitions observed in 59... actually support is outgoing transitions of source activity). A01 is new and fans out to many activities.
5. DIR002: A09 outgoing — before: A02 37.5%, A04 24%, A07 17%, A08 8%, A05 7%, A06 4%, A10 1%, A15 1%; after: A02 65%, A04 14%, A05 4%, A06 6%, A08 3%, A10 2%, A14 3%, A15 1%, A01 1%. A07 disappeared as successor (17% → 0), A02 rose from ~38% to ~65%.
6. DIR003: A14 outgoing — before: A08 63%, A12 10%, A06 5%, A19 5%, A10 5%, A11 4%, others small; after: A08 24%, A06 21%, A15 19%, A07 7%, A02 6%, A10 5%, A11 5%, A09 3%, A13 3%, A16 2%, A12 2%, A19 1%. A08 dropped from ~63% to ~24%; A15 appeared at ~19%.
7. DIR004: A18 outgoing — before: spread across A10 19%, A06 13%, A12 13%, A16 12%, A19 12%, A07 10%, A17 8%, A11 8%, A13 4%, A09 2%; after: A01 65%, rest small. A18 now leads to A01 in about 65% of its outgoing transitions.
8. POS001: A01 position — after: mean position ~0.77 (normalized?), median ~0.85, q25 0.59, q75 1.0. Before: nothing. So A01 occurs late in traces (positions near the end, if positions normalized 0–1). Actually positions are event positions; mean 0.77 of what scale? Probably normalized position. It suggests A01 occurs late in the trace.
9. REL001: A01–A18 relation — before: co-occurrence 0, B_only (A18 only) 0.405, neither 0.595; after: co-occurrence 0.475, B_before_A 0.475, neither 0.525. So in the later window, in ~48% of traces both occur, always with A18 before A01. Before, A18 occurred alone in ~40% of traces and A01 never occurred.

So the picture: A01 is a new activity (not observed before, observed in ~48% of traces after). It occurs late in traces (median position ~0.85). A18 now frequently leads to A01 (~65% of A18's outgoing transitions after, vs 0 before). A01–A18 co-occur in ~48% of traces, always A18 before A01. A01 fans out to many activities (A10, A07, A12, A16, A17, A13, A06, A11, A19, A02).

Also A02 became repeated (mean occurrences doubled, recurrence support 0 → 0.255), and A09 now leads to A02 more often (38% → 65%), A14 leads less to A08 (63% → 24%) and more to A15/A06. A08 stopped repeating (recurrence 0.2 → 0, mean 0.87 → 0.475 with stable participation).

Main hypothesis: A new activity A01 was introduced late in the process, typically after A18, and is followed by a variety of activities. This is directly supported by OCC001 (participation 0 → 47.5%), POS001 (position), DIR004 (A18 → A01 65% of outgoing), REL001 (A18 before A01 in ~48% of traces, co-occurrence 0 → 0.475), DIR001 (A01's outgoing fan-out).

Competing explanation: A01 might be a rare variant that happened to appear — but 95/200 traces is not rare. Sampling: the two windows are finite samples; could A01 have existed before at low frequency? Before support 0 out of 200 traces — if A01 occurred in 47.5% of traces after, it's very unlikely to be absent in 200 before traces unless it truly was absent or extremely rare. The empirical strength 0.995 for all items. The screening count 9 vs 0.2 expected — many times larger, so chance is ruled out as a whole.

Is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence directly shows: A01 absent before, present in ~48% of traces after, positioned late, preceded by A18, followed by many activities. That's direct relational and positional evidence. Consistent across OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR004, REL001. The competing explanation that A01 existed but was unobserved before is weak given 200 traces with zero participation — though technically zero participation only means not observed. With 200 traces, an activity with ~48% participation would essentially never be missed. So the "added activity" hypothesis is well supported.

Other differences: A02 repetitions increased (OCC002), A08 repetitions stopped (OCC003), A09's successor mix shifted toward A02 (DIR002), A14's successor mix shifted away from A08 toward A15/A06 (DIR003). These could be related to the A01 insertion (e.g., rerouting), but per instructions, report them under "Other differences" without adding to main hypothesis. Actually, are they part of the main hypothesis? The main hypothesis is about A01 being added. The A02/A08 repetition changes and A09/A14 redirection are separate differences. DIR002 and DIR003 might be consequences of rerouting around A01, but the evidence doesn't directly tie them. I'll report them as other differences.

Note the caveat: several indicators reflect the same trace behaviour — OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR004, REL001 all reflect the A01 insertion; they're not independent confirmations. But they do show different facets (participation, position, predecessor, successors, relation), which together give a direct, consistent picture.

Support level: Supported hypothesis. The evidence directly shows the change (A01 present after, absent before; A18 → A01 relation; A01's successors), consistently across five items, and the screening count (9 vs 0.2 expected) rules out chance as a whole. The main limitation: zero participation before only means A01 was not observed in the earlier window; theoretically it could have been extremely rare before, though 0/200 makes substantial prior presence unlikely. Also, we cannot tell from these data whether A01 replaced some other behaviour — but A18's outgoing transitions before went to many activities and now mostly to A01, suggesting A01 was inserted after A18.

Wait — check DIR004 more carefully: before, A18's outgoing transitions were spread across many activities (A10 19%, A06 13%, A12 13%, A16 12%, A19 12%, A07 10%, A17 8%, A11 8%, A13 4%, A09 2%). After, A01 takes 65%. So A18 previously flowed to a variety of activities and now mostly to A01. Combined with REL001 (A18 before A01 in all co-occurrences), A01 sits after A18. And A01 then fans out to A10, A07, A12, A16, A17, A13, A06, A11, A19, A02 — which overlaps with A18's previous successors (A16, A07, A06, A10, A12, A19, A17, A13, A11, A09). Interesting: A01's successor set largely mirrors A18's previous successor set. That suggests A01 was inserted between A18 and its former successors. That's a nice consistent story: A01 inserted after A18, taking over A18's outgoing edges. But I should be careful not to over-speculate. I can note that A01's outgoing transitions go to many of the activities A18 previously led to. That's descriptive, from the data.

Hmm, but the instruction says don't speculate about causes or change pattern names. Describing "A01 now leads to activities that A18 previously led to" is a data description, fine.
